reqs.title: Senior Instrumentation Designer
reqs.recruitability_rationale: Clear role, defined tool stack, defined locations with remote allowed, and a usable pay ceiling — a recruiter can start today. The only friction is the hard 'power, not O&G' filter, which meaningfully narrows the SPI-designer pool and must be honored in sourcing.
reqs.role_summary: Senior instrumentation & controls (I&C) designer producing loop/wiring/instrument drawings and directing junior designers on power-sector projects for Worley — a contract W2 seat, remote-flexible with optional office presence in Reading PA, Kansas City, or Charlotte.
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A 10-15 year I&C designer who's lived in SmartPlant Instrumentation (SPI/INtools), AutoCAD and MicroStation, with genuine power-generation or utility project experience rather than pure upstream/midstream O&G. At $100/hr W2 max, remote-eligible, this is a workable but not deep pool — the power-industry filter is the real constraint, not the rate.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Major — this one's workable today; just make sure the recruiter reads the client comment as truth: power experience is the gate and the role is remote-flexible across three offices, not onsite-Reading like the body says, and remind them to submit at requested rate under the $100 cap, not at the cap.

actions.action: Set sourcing to power-sector I&C designers (SPI + AutoCAD/MicroStation) and screen out pure O&G-only backgrounds up front, since the client explicitly excluded 'just traditional O&G.'
actions.why_it_matters: Without this filter the recruiter fills the pipe with midstream/refining designers the client will reject on first pass, burning submittals on a VMS req where win rate is already thin.

actions.action: Coach recruiters to submit at each candidate's requested rate up to the $100/hr W2 ceiling — not auto-submit at $100 — per the client comment.
actions.why_it_matters: Submitting everyone at the cap violates the stated instruction and can get OakTree's submittals deprioritized against other VMS suppliers.

actions.action: Extract the contract duration from the Airswift VMS rep — the body and header both show duration as '???'.
actions.why_it_matters: Senior contract designers screen hard on assignment length before engaging; an unknown duration slows candidate buy-in and can stall the first calls.

actions.action: Confirm with the VMS rep whether the degree/diploma in instrumentation design is a hard gate or waivable by equivalent experience (the 'Preferred' section suggests the latter).
actions.why_it_matters: Many strong senior designers came up through drafting without a formal instrumentation diploma; treating it as hard would cut real candidates.

Wants to move back to Tulsa and asked for ~$100k+ (confirmed at $105k, within the $95-105k band) — fits the Tulsa 2/3 hybrid on-site requirement and comp
fit_risks: JD requires ~6+ years of IT PM experience; resume shows IT Project Manager only since Dec 2021 (~4.5 yrs, prior roles were IT Support Specialist and Tier 2 Technician) while the submission claims 'nearly six years' — verify the true dedicated-PM YOE before interview
Background is gaming/casino industry, not insurance — not a stated must-have but a context gap the hiring manager may probe
Notes don't mention Microsoft Project or ServiceNow specifically (JD lists MS Project as frequently used and ServiceNow as the ticketing system) — confirm tool familiarity ahead of the PM assessment
JD flags a PM assessment/test and personality assessment plus a ~2-hour in-person first round — no signal yet on how he'll perform on those gates
candidates.fit_rationale: A viable, well-aligned first candidate whose Tulsa relocation, cross-functional IT delivery and in-band rate fit the role; confirming his true dedicated-PM YOE against the 6+ requirement and MS Project/ServiceNow exposure would de-risk him before the client's assessment round.

reqs.title: Recruiter
reqs.recruitability_rationale: Coherent, well-scoped role with clear skills, location, duration, and both bill and pay rates identified — a recruiter knows exactly what to search for and the pool of Houston EPC/O&G recruiters is healthy at this rate.
reqs.role_summary: A contract corporate/technical recruiter to source and pipeline engineering and EPC talent for Technip Energies' internal TA team in Houston — a hunter/sourcer role, not a staffing sales seat, sitting on-site through end of 2026 with CTH potential.
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A Houston-based agency or corporate recruiter with 2-7 years sourcing engineering/EPC/O&G talent, comfortable cold-calling passive candidates and carrying multiple reqs — the kind of person who's done agency desk work or in-house TA at Worley/KBR/Fluor. At $30-40/hr W2 on-site CTH, you're realistically landing a mid-level recruiter, not a senior TA lead, and athletic/competitive background is a culture preference not a filter.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Clean, sourceable req, Chuck — just pin down whether $40/hr is flat or a range and whether O&G experience is a hard gate or a plus, so Emily's pod isn't guessing on the first screen.

actions.action: Confirm with Walker whether the pay is a firm $40/hr flat or the $30-40 range in the JD, so recruiters set candidate expectations correctly on first call.
actions.why_it_matters: Recruiters pitching $30-40 when the client is really offering $40 (or vice versa) creates fallout and re-work at offer.

actions.action: Nail down the non-negotiables — is this strictly EPC/O&G recruiting experience required, or will strong technical/engineering agency sourcers from adjacent industries be considered?
actions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the recruiter searches a narrow O&G-only pool or a broader technical-sourcing pool, directly affecting submittal volume.

actions.action: Get the interview process from Walker — number of rounds, on-site vs virtual, and turnaround — since this is an on-site CTH the client will move fast on hunters.
actions.why_it_matters: Without the cadence, strong hunter candidates (who have options) go cold before the client schedules them.

reqs.title: Customer Service Agent
reqs.recruitability_rationale: Clear role, clear skills, hard location, both bill and pay rate documented, direct hiring-manager access with phone number — a recruiter can source this today. The only open item (req not yet officially released) is a timing/paperwork matter, not a sourcing blocker.
reqs.role_summary: Entry-level onsite call center rep taking inbound mortgage servicing calls for BOK's contract staffing — a backfill for a departing contractor, with possible (not guaranteed) conversion.
reqs.role_family: Business professional / call center — financial services customer service
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A Dallas/Irving-area call center agent with inbound phone experience, ideally some mortgage servicing or financial services exposure, comfortable onsite 5 days at ~$21.43/hr W2. Deep, easily-sourced local pool; mortgage experience is the differentiator, not a gate.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Clean, sourceable intake, Carley — just nail down whether it's officially released and the interview cadence so we don't waste any of the 3 submittal slots on a req that's still stuck in approval.

actions.action: Confirm with Maria that the req has officially released (the 8/24 note said pending approval, out 'within the week') before pushing submittals, since Ernestine's last day was 8/28 and the client wants coverage.
actions.why_it_matters: Submitting before official release risks candidates sitting idle; confirming release timing lets the recruiter time submittals to the urgent backfill need.

actions.action: Lock the hiring/interview process with Maria — number of interview rounds, format, and turnaround expectations — using her direct line (918-879-7059).
actions.why_it_matters: With a departing contractor and a 3-candidate submission cap, knowing the interview cadence lets the recruiter set candidate expectations and move fast without wasting the limited submittal slots.

actions.action: Confirm this BOK contract role runs the OSCN/BOK background, drug, and fingerprint gate and pre-screen candidates for those before submitting.
actions.why_it_matters: BOK background gates are strict; a candidate who fails after submittal burns one of only three allowed slots.

reqs.title: Process Engineer
reqs.recruitability_rationale: Coherent, well-specified senior EPC process engineer role with clear software stack (HYSYS/Aspen), clear location (Pasadena onsite/hybrid), and both bill and pay rates documented — a viable and deep Houston-market pool exists at this rate. No contradictions once the dated client comment on schedule is read as current.
reqs.role_summary: Senior (III) process engineer for an EPC — leads process design deliverables (PFDs, P&IDs, H&MBs), drives HYSYS/Aspen simulations, leads HAZOP/PHA safety reviews, and mentors juniors on mid-to-large petrochemical/refinery projects out of H+M's Pasadena office.
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A ChemE with 10-20 years in Gulf Coast EPC houses (Technip, Wood, Fluor, S&B, Jacobs, or H+M peers) who lives in Aspen HYSYS/Plus, has run process leads on petrochem/refinery projects, and has field/startup exposure. At $70-85/hr W2 in Pasadena this is a very fillable Houston-market contract profile; PE is a plus but frequently waived for strong deliverable-owning leads.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Chuck — clean, sourceable req; just tidy the 7-15 vs 7-25 mismatch and flag which Aspen tools are real gates vs. template padding so Drew's pod doesn't over-screen on the full suite.

actions.action: Reconcile the experience band — AM notes say 7-25 years, the JD says 7-15; tell the recruiter which to source to (recommend 10+ with a soft ceiling) so a strong 20-year lead isn't auto-excluded.
actions.why_it_matters: Without alignment the recruiter may screen out exactly the senior leads the role wants, or waste time on the wrong end of the band.

actions.action: Confirm with Dale whether the Aspen suite (Flarenet, EDR) and Navisworks are true must-haves or HYSYS/Plus is the real gate, and whether this is 1 or 2-3 openings per the client comment.
actions.why_it_matters: Over-stated software gates will artificially shrink a sourceable pool, and knowing 2-3 heads changes recruiter throughput.

actions.action: Confirm the pay/bill rate as documented ($70-85 pay / $91-110.50 bill) is firm and note the client's stated willingness to 'go a little above' for the right person.
actions.why_it_matters: Rates are present so sourcing can start, but locking the ceiling avoids losing a strong lead over a few dollars given the client already flagged flexibility.

submittal_intel.pipeline_summary: Single-candidate exclusive req: Rayfield May was submitted to H+M on 8/25 at a $95/hr pay rate ($123.50 bill) and is currently at Client Submission with references provided as of 8/27 — awaiting client feedback. No rejections yet, so no rejection patterns to learn from.

candidates.where_they_are: Submitted 8/25 at $95/hr PR ($123.50 BR); confirmed right-to-represent and provided references (Air Products colleagues) on 8/26-8/27 — sitting at Client Submission awaiting H+M feedback, only 4 days out so still fresh.
fit_strengths: Resume and screen show 25 years O&G process engineering across Air Products, KBR, and Stone & Webster supporting refinery, petrochemical, LNG, ammonia, hydrogen and gasification — directly matches JD's petrochemical/refinery EPC focus
Explicitly proficient in Aspen HYSYS/Plus plus UniSim — hits the AM's stated 'must be highly proficient with Aspen-HYSYS' non-negotiable

Extensive FEED-to-construction EPC experience with PFD/P&ID (SmartPlant SPID), hydraulic calculations, process design and process safety — aligns with JD's Process Engineer III deliverable and lead responsibilities
Bluebeam listed in his tech stack, matching a specific JD tool requirement
fit_risks: Submitted at $95/hr PR and $123.50 BR — above the client's stated $70-85 pay / $91-110.50 bill range; client said they could 'go a little above' but this exceeds the top of the bill band, a real negotiation risk
At 25 years he is at the very top edge of the AM's '7-25 year range' target and could read as senior/overqualified for a contract rate
Resume/notes don't explicitly confirm he can lead formal safety reviews (PHA/HAZOP/HAZID/SIL) as the JD requires — verify before interview
candidates.fit_rationale: Strong technical and industry fit that clearly hits the Aspen-HYSYS and EPC/FEED must-haves; the main thing to de-risk is the above-range rate — confirm the client will accept ~$95/hr and validate HAZOP/SIL leadership.

reqs.title: Recruiter
reqs.recruitability_rationale: Clear role, clear location, defined pay band and markup, coherent must-haves, and a deep Tulsa candidate pool at this level and rate. Only real friction is the confidential-search constraint, which is a sourcing tactic issue, not a blocker.
reqs.role_summary: Corporate in-house recruiter (contract-to-hire) backfilling a departing internal TA person at H&P's Tulsa HQ — full-cycle corporate/operational/technical recruiting, onsite, supporting a busy TA team carrying ~60 open reqs.
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A Tulsa-based recruiter with 1-3 years of full-cycle experience — likely agency or corporate TA — comfortable with ATS/high-volume req loads and willing to go fully onsite for a $28-34/hr W2 C2H. This is a plentiful pool in the Tulsa market; agency recruiters looking to move in-house are the sweet spot.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Carley — clean, sourceable req; just lock the PR off 'TBD' to the $28-34 band and make sure Emily's pod has a no-name outreach angle before they start dialing, since this is a confidential search on an Exclusive account.

actions.action: Build the confidential-search outreach script now — reach candidates on the role/scope (Tulsa corporate full-cycle recruiter, C2H, ~60-req team) without naming H&P, since intake explicitly forbids sharing the company name in initial outreach.
actions.why_it_matters: Recruiters default to leading with the client name to attract candidates; violating the confidentiality instruction risks the client relationship on an Exclusive account.

actions.action: Confirm the pay rate is landing at $28-34/hr (PR currently marked TBD in comp section) so recruiters set candidate expectations correctly out of the gate.
actions.why_it_matters: The band appears in two places but is still tagged TBD; a recruiter quoting a range that later shrinks causes candidate fallout on a C2H where comp conversion matters.

actions.action: Confirm background/drug screen scope (JD lists background checks, drug screens, physicals for candidates but doesn't state the contractor's own pre-employment gate) so no one is submitted who can't clear H&P onboarding.
actions.why_it_matters: Prevents late-stage fallout on C2H conversion if the contractor must pass the same screening they'll administer.
